headline: Making complex
feel effortless.
body: This is an internal project — a full redesign of an existing platform. Due to NDA obligations, all figures, fund names, and user data shown are illustrative mock data only.

The original Fund Portal worked, but barely felt like it. No design system, inconsistent components, a visual language borrowed from five different eras — operators learned to live with the friction rather than expect better.

The redesign started from zero: a new component library built in React, a proper token-driven design system, and a clear information hierarchy that lets users see the state of every order, fund, and position at a glance.

blocks.label: Challenge
blocks.text: An internal tool that had grown organically — no shared style, no consistent components, hard to scan and slow to act in. The team deserved an interface that matched the complexity of the work they were doing.

blocks.label: Solution
blocks.text: A ground-up redesign: design tokens for every visual decision, a component library that enforces consistency by default, and an information architecture that puts the right data one click away.

blocks.label: Results
blocks.text: A modern, cohesive portal covering order matching, fund monitoring, transactions, and portfolio analytics — one design language across every surface, built entirely in React.

heading: Under the hood — what I built.

cells.label: Component architecture
cells.text: A React component library structured around feature surfaces — shared primitives, per-route compositions, zero duplicated markup.

cells.label: Design system
cells.text: Token-driven from the ground up: color, typography scale, spacing, radius, and elevation — every value named, nothing hardcoded.

cells.label: Order matching
cells.text: Buy and sell orders are surfaced with clear status indicators — pending, matched, cancelled — so operators can act without digging for context.

cells.label: Portfolio analytics
cells.text: Holdings, allocation, and performance rendered through a single charting primitive — consistent visual grammar across every analytics view.

cells.label: Fund monitoring
cells.text: Live fund status, NAV, and AUM in a single scannable layout — designed for operators who need to assess many funds at a glance.

cells.label: Transaction history
cells.text: A filterable, sortable transaction log with enough context per row that most questions get answered without opening a detail view.

items.label: Inconsistent components
items.text: Buttons, inputs and table styles were re-implemented independently on every screen. The same element looked and behaved differently depending on which page you were on — no single source of truth.

items.label: No design system
items.text: Every colour, spacing value and font size was hardcoded ad-hoc per screen. Making a global visual change meant hunting down dozens of scattered overrides with no guarantee of completeness.

items.label: Dense, hard-to-scan data
items.text: Fund data, orders and transactions were raw tables with no visual hierarchy. Operators had to read every row to locate what they needed — a slow, error-prone ritual at the start of every work session.

items.label: Outdated visual language
items.text: The interface felt like a 2015 admin panel: no breathing room, no type hierarchy, no visual cues to guide attention. It communicated low confidence in a context where trust is everything.

statement.it: respect the people who use them.

reels.name: Orders
reels.desc: Order matching at a glance — review pending buy and sell orders, check matched status, and act without context-switching.

reels.name: Funds

reels.name: Transactions
reels.desc: Transaction history — a full, filterable log of every subscription, redemption and transfer with inline status and amounts.

reels.name: Assets
reels.desc: Portfolio analytics — aggregate holdings, sector allocation and performance composed from one shared chart primitive.
